title: September inflation rises to 3.7%, driven by high diesel prices
summary: NBC report on the September 2026 CPI (3.7 percent): diesel and oil drive the rise, inflation had been heading to target before the Iran war, wages at 3 percent trail prices, and rate hikes cannot fix an oil shock.

assertions.quote: RIGHT NOW, INFLATION IS BEING DRIVEN BY HIGHER OIL PRICES.
WE KNOW DIESEL COSTS ARE UP ABOUT 75% SINCE THE WAR WITH IRAN BEGAN.

verdicts.note: Middle distillates were hit hardest because Gulf exports are distillate-heavy; fuel oil rose 15 percent in September 2026 alone per the CPI.

US No 2 diesel went from 3.722 in Feb 2026 to 4.921 in Mar, 5.600 in May and 6.291 in Sep (+69% over the pre-war month), the jump coinciding with the March 2026 crude spike; heating oil is not in this series and the attribution rests on timing.

assertions.quote: WITH INFLATION NOW AT 3.7% YOUR WAGES ARE JUST AT 3%. SO THE GAP IS GETTING WIDER HERE
YOU CAN'T DO MUCH ABOUT THAT WITH A QUARTER POINT HIKE.

verdicts.note: Rate hikes work on demand and cannot add oil supply, though they can anchor expectations and limit second-round effects, as the Fed argued in 2022.

assertions.quote: WE WERE ACTUALLY HEADING TOWARDS THAT NUMBER EARLIER THIS YEAR. BUT THEN WITH THE IRAN WAR PRICES SHOT UP.

verdicts.note: CPI ran near 2.5 percent in late 2025 and early 2026 before energy prices spiked from March 2026.

Headline CPI fell from 3.0% (September 2025) to 2.4% in January and February 2026, then jumped to 3.3%, 3.8% and 4.2% in March-May as the gasoline index rose 24.9% in March alone; the series confirm the fall and the energy-driven rebound, while the attribution to the Iran conflict comes from outside these documents.

assertions.quote: EVERYTHING ELSE IS POPPING MONTH AFTER MONTH, YEAR AFTER YEAR.

verdicts.note: September 2026 CPI showed shelter, used cars, apparel and services all accelerating while core rose to 2.6 percent from 2.4.

assertions.quote: FOOD COMING IN FLAT 0%. THAT'S A BIT ENCOURAGING
